evidence.authoring_rules_applied: R1-R10 of capability_universe.json authoring_rules_for_probe_fragments; R10 fewest-tokens tie-break used to select operator/library forms (e.g. ++x over x++ for F03.P1; static_cast forms for F07.P2/F10.P1; std::variant for F14.P1 since it is a genuinely closed alternative set in C++; explicit ternary substitution for F12.P2 because std::optional::transform/and_then require C++23 and the frozen recipe is C++20, so R9's named substitution applies and the probe is scored PARTIAL for support purposes, though its fragment still enters the Semantic Density common-basis token/fact count per interaction_with_quality_metrics.common_basis_rule).
evidence.basis: single-language shard measurement (this worker authored only the C++ fragments for all 44 frozen probes; common-basis cross-language normalization must be finished by the runner once all 10 language shards are merged)
evidence.formula: raw_density = (explicit local semantic sites) / (lexical source tokens), summed across the 44 frozen probes for this language

normalization.caveat: This worker was assigned only the C++ language column and had no visibility into the other nine languages' raw density figures, so the 0-100 value above is a provisional self-normalized figure, not a validated cross-language percentile. Raw explicit-local-site and token counts above are the authoritative evidence for downstream aggregation.
normalization.method: provisional linear scaling for this single-language shard: normalized = min(100, round(raw_density * 500)). This transform is documented so the runner can either accept it or recompute a cross-language min-max/common-basis normalization once all 10 language shards for metric.semantic_density are merged (per capability_universe.json interaction_with_quality_metrics.common_basis_rule, which requires A-D to be computed on the probe set common to all ten languages).

evidence.site_state_convention: Per semantic_site_matrix.json, only rows in state EXPLICIT_LOCAL contribute to the Semantic Density numerator. NONLOCAL states were assigned wherever a fact required consulting a callee signature/library declaration not present in the measured fragment (notably F05.P1 bare-call aliasing/mutation facts, and F13.P1 std::stoi's failure/propagation facts, both requiring the external callee's declared signature). IMPLICIT was assigned wherever C++ imposes a default/UB behavior with no local syntactic marker (e.g. signed integer overflow under the frozen non-checked C++ recipe per toolchain_binding.safety_mode_clause, unguarded operator[] bounds behavior, silent stream-open failure). ABSENT was assigned where the frozen semantic proposition does not meaningfully occur for that fragment (e.g. no conversion in F07.P1, no failure path in F09.P1).
support_and_scoreability_notes: F12.P2 uses the R9 named substitution (explicit ternary in place of optional-aware chaining) because C++20, the frozen recipe, lacks std::optional::transform/and_then (added in C++23). The fragment is still fully measured for Semantic Density per the common-basis rule.
F14.P1 uses std::variant<Circle,Rect>, which is a genuinely closed alternative set in C++, so this is FULL support, not a substitution.
F14.P3 and F18.P2 use the frozen multi-unit recipes from toolchain_binding.multi_unit_recipes (two translation units), per spec, and this is not a P-b/P-e deviation.

F08.P1 uses the plain '+' operator because C++20 provides no standard checked/wrapping/saturating signed-integer arithmetic operation (rungs i-iii unavailable); this is documented as a language fact, not an instrument defect.
evidence.tokenizer_rule: Language-neutral punctuation-and-identifier tokenizer: each identifier, keyword, numeric/string literal, and each individual punctuation/operator glyph (including each angle bracket, colon of ::, parenthesis, brace, bracket, comma, semicolon) counts as one token. Comments and whitespace are not counted. #include directives counted as a small fixed token run. This is applied identically across all 44 probes for this language.
evidence.toolchain_recipe_used: clang++ -std=c++20 -O2 FILE.cpp -o BIN (per capability_universe.json toolchain_binding.recipes.C++; multi-unit recipe used for F14.P3 and F18.P2 per toolchain_binding.multi_unit_recipes)
